---
title: "Solomon four-group study: analysis"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(solomonR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "")
```

This document runs a Solomon four-group analysis in the order of its
pre-specified plan. It runs as written on the package's example data.
Replace the data and the plan's descriptions with your own; if your columns
have other names, name them in each call (for example,
`fit_solomon_glm(score2, group, took_pretest, score1, data = d)`).

## 1. The analysis plan

Write and register the plan before the outcomes are seen
(`?analysis_plan_solomon`). The same object is passed to the report in the
last step, which then states whether the sensitization analysis was
pre-specified.

```{r plan}
plan <- analysis_plan_solomon(
  outcome = "[the primary outcome]",
  treatment = "[the treatment, and the control condition]",
  sensitization = "test"
)
# print(plan) shows the Markdown; analysis_plan_solomon(..., file = "plan.md") saves it.
```

## 2. The data

The columns are `y_post` (posttest), `treat` (1 = treatment), `pretested`
(1 = pretested), and `y_pre` (pretest, `NA` in the unpretested groups).

```{r data}
d <- solomon_example # Replace with your data.
```

## 3. Check the design

```{r design}
validate_solomon(y_post, treat, pretested, y_pre, data = d)
check_solomon_missing(y_post, treat, pretested, y_pre, data = d)
```

## 4. Describe the baseline

Only the pretested groups have a pretest. The difference is described, not
tested, and it does not change the planned model.

```{r baseline}
baseline_solomon(y_pre, treat, pretested, data = d)
```

## 5. The planned model

```{r model}
fit <- fit_solomon_glm(y_post, treat, pretested, y_pre, data = d)
fit
plot_solomon_effects(fit)
```

If the plan tests that sensitization is negligible
(`sensitization = "equivalence"`), run the equivalence test here with the
bound the plan fixed:

```{r equivalence, eval = FALSE}
equivalence_solomon(fit, bounds = 3) # The plan's equivalence_bound.
```

## 6. Sensitivity analysis for missing posttests

This step runs only when posttests are missing. The groups shifted follow
the plan.

```{r sensitivity}
if (anyNA(d$y_post)) {
  tp <- tipping_point_solomon(y_post, treat, pretested, y_pre,
                              groups = plan$settings$tipping_groups, seed = 1, data = d)
  print(tp)
  plot_tipping_point(tp)
} else {
  cat("No posttests are missing.\n")
}
```

## 7. Report

```{r report}
report_solomon(fit, design = list(plan = plan))
```
